title: finding(scripts): the `DEBT_ISSUE` anchor pin defends the SPELLING, not the BEHAVIOUR — `= 0` satisfies its digit regex while being FALSY, so the stale-entry tail the pin exists to protect turns off with all 24 pins green
body:
Dedup keywords: `DEBT_ISSUE` · falsy anchor · pin regex · zero sentinel · spec-symbol ledger

Surfaced by the `os-dev` seat measuring objectui#9537 and **re-verified on the tree** by the `domain:ui` execution seat before filing. ⛔ Unassigned and ungraded. Class **(a)** — a reproducible defect with a measured reproduction, ⛔ not a reasoned one.

## The reading

`scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-plugin-detail-7265.test.ts:279` pins the anchor:

```
it('`DEBT_ISSUE` is still declared — an empty ledger keeps its anchor', () => {
  expect(gateText()).toMatch(/^const DEBT_ISSUE = \d+;$/m);
```

The pin's own stated purpose, quoted from its comment, is that deleting the anchor *"would silently turn the stale-entry message's tail off (it is written behind a `DEBT_ISSUE ?` guard), which is the instruction a re-seeded ledger would need most."*

⇒ the assertion is about **behaviour** (the guard stays on). The regex tests a **spelling** (it is a decimal number). Those are not the same predicate, and the gap is reachable:

| value | satisfies `/^const DEBT_ISSUE = \d+;$/m` | truthy at runtime | guard state |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `9999` | ✅ | ✅ | on |
| `null` | ❌ (pin catches it) | ❌ | — |
| **`0`** | ✅ **passes** | ❌ **falsy** | ⛔ **off, silently** |

`0` is a decimal digit, so it matches; `0` is falsy, so `DEBT_ISSUE ? … : ""` takes the empty branch and the stale-entry tail disappears — **the exact outcome the pin says it exists to prevent, with the pin green.**

## Reproduction — measured, ⛔ not reasoned

Mutate the gate to `const DEBT_ISSUE = 0;` and run `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-plugin-detail-7265.test.ts`:

- **24 passed, exit 0.** All pins green.
- Control legs from the same matrix, proving the instrument fires: `= null` → **1 failed / 23 passed**, on this very pin; the anchor-free message shape → **1 failed / 23 passed** on its sibling pin.

⇒ the pin discriminates `null` from a number, and ⛔ does not discriminate a truthy anchor from a falsy one.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

It changes the **cost of a repair that is currently under consideration** on objectui#9537. An implementer told to "retire the anchor" has a spelling available (`0`) that slips past the pin instead of amending it honestly — so the governance step the pin was built to force (amend a deliberate assertion in the open) can be skipped by accident rather than by intent.

## Ask

Tighten the pin so it asserts what its comment claims — an anchor that is **present and truthy** — and keep the `null` leg green as a control. ⚠️ Separately, the pin's **comment** and its **regex** disagree about what is protected ("still declared" vs "is a decimal number"); fix the comment too, otherwise the next reader re-derives the same wrong invariant even after the regex is tightened.

⛔ This card does ⛔ **not** decide objectui#9537's shape question (retire / re-anchor / anchor-free / out-of-gate). It is the gate blind-spot repair, which is a strengthening and stands whichever way that ruling goes.
